official.deadline_note: The scholarship application must be accompanied by an Estonian higher education institution confirmation letter of admission for 2026/27, so each institution's own admission application deadlines effectively fall earlier; those institutional deadlines are not published on the Board's scholarship pages.
official.application_cycle: 2026/2027 academic year; applications accepted in the 2026 application round (1 October - 31 October 2026)
official.status_note: The Board's page states the 2026 application period is open from 1 October 2026 until 31 October 2026 (23:59 Estonian time); the English page was last updated 06.10.2026 and the Estonian guidelines page 30.09.2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Board publishes the monthly rates and states plainly that 'other costs are not covered' (Estonian guidelines: 'Muid kulusid ei kaeta'); no tuition fee support is included in this scholarship.
benefits: the rate of the scholarship for first-cycle (BA level) higher education and master's studies is 350 euros per month
the rate of the doctoral scholarship is 660 euros per month
The scholarship is paid from the first day of studies until the last day of studies according to the dates approved by the host higher education institution

An exchange student is paid a scholarship during the period of studying in Estonia, but not more than ten (10) calendar months a year; the scholarship is paid for exchange studies lasting more than one month
Scholarships are paid to undergraduate students for 12 months of the academic year, except for the final nominal year when the scholarship is paid for 10 months
eligibility: Applications will be accepted only from students from countries whose citizenship is in one of the countries listed: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belgium, Brazil, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Czech Republic, Cyprus, Egypt, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, Great Britain, Greece, Hungary, India, Indonesia, Israel, Italy, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Lithuania, Mexico, Moldova, People's Republic of China, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Republic of Korea, Slovenia, Spain, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Tunisia, Turkey, Ukraine, United States of America

The scholarship supports master's and PhD studies in all fields; in the first stage of higher education (BA) the scholarship can only be applied for in fields that are related to Estonian language and culture
The application should include a confirmation letter concerning the student's admission to an Estonian higher education institution with reference to the 2026/27 academic year
On doctoral level, students with an active junior researcher employment contract with the Estonian HEI are not eligible for the scholarship
Degree studies scholarship applicant from 2nd year upwards has to be enrolled in full time studies

Based on the guidelines of the Ministry of Education and Research of the Republic of Estonia, applications from candidates who are citizens of the Russian Federation or Belarus will not be accepted in the application round for the 2026/2027 academic year
requirements: The application is submitted in English
The application form cannot be changed, and the form must be sent to the email address in word format. It is not necessary to sign it. Additional documents can be in PDF or other format
All submitted documents must be in English or Estonian; documents in other languages shall be submitted with the translation to one of these languages

All documents must be attached to the email; documents signed on paper are submitted scanned, and the Education and Youth Board has the right to check the conformity of the submitted documents with the originals
Applications that are incomplete, drafted offhand, include false information, omit relevant information or have been submitted after the deadline will not be considered for assessment
Applications that don't have attached a confirmation letter of admission to an Estonian higher education institution, by the application deadline, will not be processed
documents: Application form in Word format (Degree_exhange study APPLCIATION FORM 2026.docx, published by the Education and Youth Board)
A copy of your passport or ID card

Estonian higher education institution confirmation letter containing information about: degree or exchange student status in 2026/27 academic year; level of study; curriculum; start and end date of study
PhD level applicants: the confirmation letter should contain proof that you do not have an active (junior) researcher employment contract with the Estonian HEI
Degree studies scholarship applicants enrolled before the 2025/26 academic year: the confirmation letter should contain proof that you are studying full-time during the 2025/26 academic year
selection_criteria: Applications shall be evaluated based on the applicant's motivation (based on the letter of motivation) and the overall quality of the application; these two criteria carry equal weight

Applications shall be evaluated and the proposal for awarding the scholarship shall be made by the scholarship committee, based on the provisions of the directive and the committee's rules of procedure
The scholarship recipients shall be approved by a directive of the Director General of the Board
The scholarship programme is highly competitive: historically only about 10% of applicants receive the scholarship each year, and in the 2026 application round 15 scholarships will be awarded
coverage: the rate of the scholarship for first-cycle (BA level) higher education and master's studies is 350 euros per month
the rate of the doctoral scholarship is 660 euros per month
other costs are not covered (tuition, living costs and travel are not paid by this scholarship)
The scholarship is paid from the first day of studies until the last day of studies according to the dates approved by the host higher education institution
For exchange students the scholarship is paid during the period of studying in Estonia, but not more than ten (10) calendar months a year, and only for exchange studies lasting more than one month
application_method: Complete the Education and Youth Board's Word application form (Degree_exhange study APPLCIATION FORM 2026.docx); the form cannot be changed, must be sent in word format and need not be signed

Prepare a copy of your passport or ID card and the Estonian higher education institution confirmation letter with the required content (degree or exchange student status for 2026/27, level of study, curriculum, start and end date of study)

Send one email with the three annexes attached as separate files to the Education and Youth Board, entitled 'Scholarship for degree and exchange study in Estonia', within the period of 1 October until 31 October 2026 (by 23:59 Estonian time)
The application email is for submitting complete applications only
official.application_route: Email the Board's Word application form plus passport/ID copy and Estonian HEI admission confirmation letter to the Education and Youth Board during 1-31 October 2026 (one email, subject 'Scholarship for degree and exchange study in Estonia')
official.study_mode: full-time - degree studies scholarship applicants from 2nd year upwards have to be enrolled in full time studies
official.citizenship_residency: Applications accepted only from students whose citizenship is in one of the countries listed by the Board; citizens of the Russian Federation or Belarus are not accepted in the 2026/2027 round
official.international_eligibility: Only foreign nationals may apply - the programme is offered by the Ministry of Education and Research and the Education and Youth Board to foreign students, researchers and academic staff
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Master's and PhD studies are supported in all fields; at the first stage of higher education (BA) the scholarship can only be applied for in fields related to Estonian language and culture
official.duration: One academic year (2026/2027); paid for 12 months of the academic year for undergraduate students except the final nominal year (10 months); exchange students not more than ten calendar months a year
official.description: The Estonian Ministry of Education and Research and the Education and Youth Board offer scholarships to foreign nationals pursuant to bilateral intergovernmental or inter-ministerial agreements, offered since 2016 within the framework of the Estonian Scholarship Programme for international students, researchers and academic staff. This strand supports foreign students in degree or exchange study at Estonian higher education institutions in the 2026/2027 academic year, paid as a monthly scholarship of 350 euros at bachelor's and master's level and 660 euros at doctoral level.
official.program_type: Government scholarship - Estonian Scholarship Programme for international students, researchers and academic staff
official.english_requirement: The application is submitted in English; all submitted documents must be in English or Estonian, and documents in other languages must be submitted with translations into English or Estonian. No English proficiency test score is published for this strand.

not_confirmed: No English proficiency test score (IELTS/TOEFL or equivalent) is published for this strand - only the language rules for the application and its documents
Institution-specific admission application deadlines at the Estonian higher education institutions are not published on the Board's scholarship pages
The exact monthly amount actually disbursed to the student is not published; the Board transfers the scholarship to the host university, which arranges the onward payment
verification.notes: The 350 EUR/month (BA and master's) and 660 EUR/month (doctoral) rates, the 'other costs are not covered' exclusion, the 15-award 2026 round, the 1-31 October 2026 window and the required annexes were confirmed on both the English scholarship page and the Estonian-language guidelines page on harno.ee (last updated 06.10.2026 and 30.09.2026).

applicant_utility.summary: This is a modest monthly stipend - 350 EUR at bachelor's and master's level, 660 EUR at doctoral level - routed through your Estonian host university, so you must already hold a 2026/2027 admission confirmation when the 1-31 October 2026 window opens. The Board states plainly that other costs are not covered, so tuition, travel and most living expenses stay with you, and only 15 awards are expected in the 2026 round against a historic success rate of roughly one in ten. Treat it as a monthly top-up that strengthens your overall funding case, not as a fully funded study plan.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's or PhD applicants from the listed countries who already hold an Estonian HEI admission letter for 2026/27, study full-time and have separate funding for tuition and living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Get the Estonian HEI confirmation letter first - it must state 2026/27 degree or exchange student status, level of study, curriculum and exact start and end dates; applications without it are not processed at all
Download the Board's 2026 Word application form, fill it without changing its structure, and email it as a .docx (not PDF), unsigned
PhD applicants: have the confirmation letter explicitly state that you hold no active (junior) researcher employment contract with the Estonian HEI
Continuing degree students: have the letter confirm full-time study for the relevant academic year
Translate anything not already in English or Estonian, and attach all three annexes as separate files to one single email
Send before 23:59 Estonian time on 31 October 2026 with the exact subject line 'Scholarship for degree and exchange study in Estonia' - late or partial submissions are not assessed
common_rejection_risks: No Estonian HEI confirmation letter attached by the deadline - the Board will not process such applications
Citizenship problems: applicants from countries outside the published list are ineligible, and Russian or Belarusian citizens are excluded from the 2026/2027 round entirely
An altered application form, a PDF conversion of the Word form, or annexes sent later in a separate email
A weak motivation letter - it carries equal weight with the overall quality of the application
Assuming the scholarship secures your study place - it does not; the HEI admission decision must come first and the final scholarship decision follows confirmation of admission
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees, travel to Estonia, accommodation and general living costs ('other costs are not covered'), plus residence-permit, insurance and translation expenses; 350 EUR a month does not approach these, so budget them independently.
document_audit: The confirmation letter is decisive - verify all four required elements: 2026/27 degree or exchange status, level of study, curriculum, and start and end date of study
PhD letters need the explicit statement that no active junior researcher employment contract exists; a generic admission letter fails this check
The Board reserves the right to check documents against originals, so passport/ID scans must be legible and unedited
Any document in another language needs a translation into English or Estonian; unsigned scans of any signed papers are acceptable
alerts: Only 15 awards in the 2026 round with a historic ~10% success rate - the Board itself advises considering other funding sources and not relying solely on this competition
Your real timing pressure is the Estonian HEI's own admission timeline: the confirmation letter must be in your hands before the 31 October 2026 scholarship deadline
BA applicants are restricted to Estonian language and culture-related fields; master's and doctoral applicants can study any field
Degree applicants from the 2nd year upwards must be enrolled full-time, and the Estonian guidelines expect 75% cumulative curriculum completion by the end of the preceding academic year

If you do not start or continue studying in Estonia you lose the right to the scholarship, and changing the scholarship period afterwards needs the Board's written consent and never increases the total
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One email with three attached files (Word application form, passport/ID copy, Estonian HEI confirmation letter) to the Board's application address during 1-31 October 2026; the Board pays the host university, which disburses the monthly scholarship, and results are announced personally by email.
